question: What is the air quality in Singapore right now?
name: Claude
answer:
Air quality in Singapore is poor right now because of haze from fires in Indonesia. The latest reading I found is from 10am on Friday, Oct 16, and it puts three regions in the "very unhealthy" range.

**Latest readings (24-hour PSI)**
- **Central:** entered the very unhealthy range at midnight and hit 227 at 9am, a new high for the year. At 10am, it dipped to 226 while readings in the east and west entered the very unhealthy band at 202 and 201, respectively.
- **North and South:** Readings in the other two regions were at the unhealthy level – 150 in the north and 183 in the south.
- **Hourly PM2.5:** The hourly PM2.5 readings in the central and western regions were in the high band, at 164 and 158, respectively, while readings in the other regions were elevated, ranging from 96 to 141.

**What the numbers mean:** On the PSI scale, Good 0–50 Moderate 51–100 Unhealthy 101–200 Very Unhealthy 201–300 Hazardous >300.

**Health advice:** When the 24-hour PSI is very unhealthy, NEA's guidance is:
- Healthy persons: Avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion
- Elderly, pregnant women, children: Minimise outdoor activity
- Persons with chronic lung or heart disease: Avoid outdoor activity

**Cause:** Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Thursday that Singapore is looking into which companies may be responsible for the forest and peatland fires in Indonesia that have caused the worsening haze. The haze got worse quickly this week. On Wednesday, 1-hour PM2.5 readings spiked around the country, with the reading in the west rising to a level not seen in Singapore since 2015.

The readings change every hour, so for the most current numbers, check NEA's haze.gov.sg website or the myENV app.

SINGAPORE, Sept 27 — Air quality has been gradually deteriorating throughout the day, with the 3-hour PSI mark breaching the 100 mark at 2pm today.

As at 6pm, the 24-hour PSI was still in the moderate range at 82-92, while the three-hour PSI was at 145. 
The National Environment Agency (NEA) said in a 5pm update today that the 24-hour PSI over the next 24 hours is expected to be in the low to mid-sections of the unhealthy range, with a possibility of entering the high-section of the Unhealthy range if denser haze is blown in by unfavourable winds. 
Moderate to dense haze is still persisting in central and southern Sumatra, and some haze has spread to the sea areas west and south of Singapore, said the NEA.

The NEA advised healthy persons to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor physical exertion.

Singapore’s National Environment Agency said the pollutant standards index (PSI) breached the unhealthy level of 100 today, hitting 111 in an eastern suburb and 102 in the island’s centre before midday.

At PSI levels between 100 and 200, residents are advised to “reduce prolonged strenuous outdoor physical exertion”, according to NEA guidelines.

However, people were still seen jogging and cycling in one park in the city’s east.



The agency said late yesterday that the number of fire “hotspots” on the nearby Indonesian island of Sumatra had surged to 212, up from 65 on Thursday and 15 Wednesday.

“Smoke plumes and haze were observed from satellite imagery over southern and central Sumatra. A brief shift in the wind direction... blew some of the lighter haze toward Singapore and caused a deterioration in air quality,” it added.

Malaysia has also been affected, with the country’s top environment official last week blaming Indonesian forest fires for the haze.

The Indonesian environment minister, however, has denied any transboundary haze.
